atoms.b: Celtic homes were very simple. People typically lived in roundhouses, which were circular huts made from ((++natural synthetic)) materials such as wood, straw and clay.

In contrast, wealthy Romans lived in villas, which were big and beautifully decorated ((++stone straw)) houses with many rooms and gardens. Some families even had private bathhouses and intricate mosaics!

feedback.finish: As Roman rule continued, some wealthy Britons also began living in Roman-style villas.

instruction.text: Select all the objects that do not belong in a Roman villa.

feedback.finish: The Romans lived without electricity and depended on oil lamps, fires and human labour to carry out daily tasks.

atoms.text: Some Roman villas had an underfloor heating system called a hypocaust, which involved lighting a fire in an underground furnace. This created hot air that circulated around small chambers beneath the floor, heating the rooms above.
atoms.sound: Some Roman villas had an underfloor heating system called a hypeocaust, which involved lighting a fire in an underground furnace. This created hot air that circulated around small chambers beneath the floor, heating the rooms above.

atoms.text: Hypocausts were expensive to build and were usually kept running by enslaved people, so they were mainly found in wealthy homes and public bathhouses.
